files.note: Changed between the releases: getUserByEmail's shape rule moved to TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN in src/constants.ts, with the comment that argued for it; the rule itself is unchanged. The claim now names the constant, and leaves the rationale to that file.

sources.supports: Every method validates its identifier and places it as the path segment of the matching endpoint. getUserByEmail checks the address against TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN, a deliberately loose shape rule, one @ with non-empty whitespace-free parts, and refuses anything else before dispatch. getUsers takes an optional project and addresses get_users/{project_id} when it is given. updateGroup injects the path identifier into the body as group_id, overwriting whatever the caller supplied, because TestRail rejects a body without it. No write payload is parsed by a public method, so every payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.

get_group and get_groups return a group and an envelope of groups. add_group takes name and user_ids; update_group supports the same fields and states that a supplied user_ids sets the group's members to match it exactly, with no way to add or remove one member. delete_group returns no group data.

input_policy.notes: One identifier in the path and no request body at all, so every field beyond it is refused.

outer_result.notes: The method resolves with no value and the wrapper reports data: null, which matches TestRail's statement that this endpoint returns no group data. The users in the group are not deleted; they stop belonging to it. The two group writes carry a TestRail 7.5 requirement from the driver's payload comment; neither that comment nor TestRail's reference states one for this endpoint, so none is claimed.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Send exactly one request. The adapter never follows up with further calls to find or repair what the deletion removed.

parameters.semantics: The group to delete. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as the only path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.
